$comment: X-MUX AASIST-L fine-tuning configuration example. This is a TEMPLATE for the offline training workspace (GPU host). Training never runs on Vercel; the serving backend only loads the finished artifact. Fill in real paths after datasets are acquired and licenses verified. See training/README.md for the full workflow.

run.notes: Baseline-then-finetune run; augment both classes equally; unseen-generator split mandatory.

base_model.output_contract: (B,2) logits; evidence = softmax col 0 (spoof); protocol score = col 1 (bonafide)

data.$comment_unseen: Mandatory: at least 2 generator families entirely excluded from train and val. Seen vs unseen results are reported separately, never combined.

augmentation.$comment_augmentation: Goal: prevent 'clean=genuine, compressed=fake' shortcuts. Motivated by the observed (informal, single-sample) false positive on a band-limited genuine 1963 broadcast recording during development.

hyperparameters.$comment_learning_rate: 1e-5 is deliberately LOW because this is fine-tuning from a pretrained checkpoint, not training from scratch; adjust on validation data only.
hyperparameters.$comment_resources: Memory/duration depend on model, input length, batch size, precision, optimizer and GPU. Never promise exact VRAM or wall-clock figures — measure on your host.

thresholds.$comment_thresholds: Every reported metric must state dataset, split (seen/unseen), threshold and model version.

calibration.$comment_calibration: null = skip for now. Set to 'platt' or 'isotonic' AFTER baseline validation. Fit on held-out validation data ONLY — never on test, never on train. Keep raw score, calibrated score and application risk separate.

export.$comment_export: PyTorch checkpoint is the primary artifact (loaded via XMUX_AASIST_MODEL_PATH). ONNX may be produced only after verified parity tests on a fixed probe set.
